When Should Your Child See an Orthodontist? You don't always have to wait until all of your child's permanent teeth have erupted before seeing an orthodontist. For some children, an orthodontic evaluation between 6 and 10 years of age can help identify growth and bite concerns at an important stage of development. Look out for signs such as: Mouth breathing or frequent snoring Crowded or misplaced teeth Crossbite A narrow upper jaw Concerns with the bite or jaw growth Early evaluation doesn't necessarily mean your child needs braces. It allows an orthodontist to monitor development and, when appropriate, guide jaw growth or use expansion while your child is still growing. If something doesn't look right with your child's bite, jaw, teeth, or breathing, don't wait for all the permanent teeth to come in. An early checkup can help identify problems while there is still an opportunity to guide growth. Want to know the 5 signs your child may need an orthodontic checkup? Does your jaw hurt, click, or feel stiff? It might not be "just your jaw." 👀 TMJ pain is often linked to habits you don't even realize you're doing every day. 🦷 **Poor posture**especially looking down at your phone or laptop for hours can put extra strain on the muscles and joints that support your jaw. 😬 **Teeth clenching or grinding**whether during the day or while you sleep places excessive pressure on the TMJ, leading to pain, headaches, facial muscle soreness, and difficulty opening or closing your mouth. If you've been experiencing: ✔️ Jaw pain or tenderness ✔️ Clicking or popping sounds ✔️ Frequent headaches ✔️ Pain while chewing ✔️ A feeling that your jaw gets "stuck" ...it's worth getting evaluated rather than ignoring it. #TMJ #JawPain #Dentist #DentalCare #OralHealth Teeth Grinding Bruxism Posture Matters Healthy Smile Dental Clinic

Here's what can happen if you keep using an old toothbrush: 🦷 Your teeth don't get cleaned as effectively. 🦷 Plaque can build up more easily. 🦷 Your risk of cavities and gum problems may increase. 🦷 Stains and bad breath can become more noticeable. A simple rule to remember: ✅ Replace your toothbrush (or electric toothbrush head) every 3 months. ✅ Change it sooner if the bristles are frayed. ✅ Replace it after recovering from a cold, flu, or other illness. A new toothbrush takes just a minute to replace, but it can make a big difference to your daily oral hygiene and long-term dental health. When was the last time you changed yours? 🪥✨ #DentalCare #Toothbrush #OralHygiene #HealthySmile #DentistTips DentalHealth SmileCare OralHealth

"Do braces or aligners cause TMJ problems? The answer is: No." Braces and clear aligners do not cause TMJ/TMD. Research has consistently shown that orthodontic treatment is not a cause of temporomandibular disorders (TMD). If someone develops jaw pain during treatment, it's usually because TMD is a common condition that can appear with or without braces. Factors like stress, teeth grinding (bruxism), muscle overuse, previous jaw injuries, and existing joint issues are much more likely contributors. Orthodontic treatment is designed to improve your bite and smile—not to cause TMJ disorders. If you have jaw pain, clicking, or difficulty opening your mouth, don't panic. A proper evaluation can identify the real cause and guide the right treatment. Don't let myths stop you from getting the smile you deserve.
